summary.intent: Get a status on the caliper v1-alpha work after a session restart, hand off to a fresh lead session, land PR #490's findings fix, open change 291's PR, and work out why dependabot and all other PRs fail CI.
summary.outcome: #490 and #492 merged via the other lead session. The converter-memo branch (change 291) was found to have been pushed with the wrong commit, so I fast-forwarded it to the real work and PR #499 now exists. The cause of the red CI was traced to cargo-deny advisories on main, and a worker was dispatched to fix them in deny.toml; that fix is unverified.

repo: Entire opens PRs only when a linked branch has a diff against main; a branch sitting at a main commit never gets a PR.
The CI aggregate job fails via `exit 1` whenever an upstream job fails, so the real failure is in the upstream job such as Audit (cargo deny).

Audit (cargo deny) is red on main and on every PR because of two new RustSec advisories: humantime unmaintained (RUSTSEC-2026-0542) and xattr unsound (RUSTSEC-2026-0486), both pulled in through watchexec.
Dependabot PR #496 is a 20-package npm group bump that also breaks Node 24/26 tests, Vite plugin tests and coverage.
Entire Gates fails on dependabot PRs and on release PR #497; the cause was not investigated.
Worker pre-push gate: lint, doc-check, machete, typos, nextest, test-checker-lane, a awaited /code-review medium, mutation proofs and a grammar sweep.
Entire findings on a change are resolved by the lead after a verified fix, citing the commit and test.

code.finding: Entire finding on change 291: `enum Level { Low = 1 << 2 }` with --no-checker yields the string "Low" instead of 4. This is probably a bug already on main and is unconfirmed.
Edited by a worker to upgrade or ignore the failing advisories, with a reason and a 30-day review-by date per ignore.

workflow: Verify a pushed SHA with `git ls-remote` and `git diff --stat origin/main...<sha>` before reporting a branch as pushed. A wrong local branch was pushed and reported as done.
Two lead sessions on the same branches race on pushes, findings and worktree edits. Hand off ownership explicitly and have the other session confirm.
A subagent that is resumed and a new lead can both edit one worktree and overwrite each other's files, as happened with the `.orig` restore.
Playwright MCP servers outlive their use and can open browser windows. Killing them can disconnect the current session's own Playwright tools.
Peer and subagent messages carry no user authority, so release actions, opening PRs through the shim (Touch ID) and risk decisions stay with the user.

friction: The session restart left the #490 worker mid-task, and the new lead session and the resumed worker both edited the same worktree.
I reported the converter-memo branch as pushed with a 324 MiB saving when the pushed commit was a main commit with no diff, so Entire never opened a PR.
Mystery browser windows appeared and the cause could not be pinned down. Stopping Playwright MCP servers disconnected my own Playwright tools.
The sandbox hid some exit codes, so a git ancestor check had to be read from its output.
Every PR was red from the Audit check on main, which blocked dependabot automation.
The worker skipped some gates after its last review fix, so CI is the first run of those.
open_items: Fix cargo-deny Audit on main: the worker is editing deny.toml, and I still need to review its report, push, link, and merge main into PRs #493, #499, #500, #501 and #502.
Confirm and fix the enum `1 << 2` evaluation bug at resolver/named.rs:609-614 as a separate slice if Entire keeps the finding open on #499.
Diagnose why Entire Gates fails on #497 and on the dependabot PRs.
Split the 20-package npm dependabot group (#496) and decide on a policy for advisories and auto-merging dependabot; the advisory-ignore decision belongs to the user.
Rule changes still to do: change 8 (MUI .d.ts components keep className/style/ref), change 7 (hook hand-offs as forwarding), and the Chakra fixture at about 865 rows.

User decisions pending: the 0.11.0 release recovery and whether #497 is the vehicle, whether the addon default flip ships in the first alpha, the alpha audience, and whether the 50% coverage floor stays.
After merges, run the oracle once on merged main and refresh the docs/STATUS.md speed numbers.
Check the post-merge CI results of #490 and #492, which have not been looked at.
